 Air New Zealand Prepares for 850,000 School Holiday Travellers
 Air New Zealand Adds Seats During School Holiday Period
 Air New Zealand is preparing to carry around 850,000 customers across its domestic and international networks during the school holiday period, which runs from 24 September to 11 October.
 More than 520,000 customers are expected to travel domestically, while almost 330,000 are travelling internationally during the holiday period. The airline expects more than 32,000 customers to travel on both 2 and 9 October.
 To meet demand, Air New Zealand has added seats on selected routes. Compared with the same holiday period last year, capacity has increased by 23% between Auckland and Sydney, 10% between Auckland and Queenstown, and 12% between Auckland and Brisbane.
 Air New Zealand School Holiday Travel
 Close to 150,000 customers are expected to travel to and from South Island destinations including Queenstown, Nelson and Dunedin during the break.
 More than 170,000 customers are travelling to and from Australia, with Sydney, Brisbane and Melbourne among the key destinations. Air New Zealand has also added nearly 1,000 seats for travel around the Bledisloe Cup in Sydney on 17 October, including two additional return services between Auckland and Sydney.
 More than 50,000 customers are heading to Pacific destinations, with Rarotonga, Nadi and Apia among the destinations seeing demand. For long-haul travel, Singapore, Japan and Los Angeles are among the destinations being travelled to.
 Kate Boyer Kate Boyer, Air New Zealand Chief Operations Officer – Ground and Inflight , said: “We’ll have families heading away, kids flying on their own to see grandparents, people travelling for some big events, and plenty of Kiwi making the most of the break. Behind the scenes, thousands of our people will be working across the network to keep everything moving, and we’re looking forward to getting everyone where they need to be.”
 She added: “The teams have been preparing for weeks for school holidays. Our goal is to sustain our recent strong on time performance even through this busy period – and that takes careful preparation and teamwork.”
 Air New Zealand Advises Travellers to Check Baggage Allowance
 With flights busy during the school holiday period, Air New Zealand is encouraging passengers to check their cabin baggage allowance before travelling.
 “Overhead locker space can be pretty tight on busy flights, so we encourage customers to check they are within limits before they leave home. Economy customers should make sure their main carry-on bag is within the 7kg allowance, and if you’re taking more, it’s best to organize checked baggage before you travel to avoid having to re-pack at the airport,” said Boyer.
 Activities for Young Travellers
 Air New Zealand has also brought back its Kia Ora Kids magazine onboard, featuring activities for younger passengers.
 The airline’s Plane Spotter’s Guide is also available for children interested in aviation. The free guide includes illustrations, spotting clues and facts about aircraft in the Air New Zealand fleet, including ATRs, Q300s, Airbus aircraft, Dreamliners and 777s.
